headline: New law raises pay for Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees, extends Chapter 11 quarterly fees, and keeps temporary bankruptcy judgeships for five more years.
what_it_does: The law increases the amount paid from case fees to trustees who handle Chapter 7 (liquidation) bankruptcy cases. It extends for five more years the quarterly fees that businesses in Chapter 11 (reorganization) cases pay to the U.S. trustee, and raises the fee percentage for cases that pay out large amounts, within limits. It also extends temporary bankruptcy judge positions in several court districts for five more years.

who_it_affects.how: They will receive larger payments from case fees for handling liquidation cases.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and others filing Chapter 11 bankruptcy
who_it_affects.how: They will keep paying quarterly fees to the U.S. trustee for five more years, and those with large payouts may pay a higher percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Federal bankruptcy courts in certain districts
who_it_affects.how: Temporary bankruptcy judgeships that were set to expire will continue for five more years.

who_it_affects.group: People and businesses with cases in affected bankruptcy courts
who_it_affects.how: Their cases will continue to be heard by courts that keep their current number of judges.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 6, 2026; the summary does not give specific start dates for each change.
